notes.claim: The square root symbol writes the exact side length of a square whose area is a given number of square units, such as 73.
A surd is an expression that includes a square root, cube root or other root symbol.
A rounded decimal answer such as 1.73 is not exact, so an exact answer is left as a surd.

sources.title: 8.1.2: Side Lengths and Areas - Mathematics LibreTexts
sources.quote: But we want to be able to talk about its exact length. In order to write “the side length of a square whose area is 73 square units,” we use the square root symbol.
